_note: SAMPLE. Generated from the hypothesised draft so the pages can be built and reviewed before Thursday. Replaced by live data on draft day.

roast.text: Keshia took the best player on the board with nobody better sitting there, which is the first time all year she's done something we can't argue with. We're logging it as a mistrigger. Josh Allen at three, and the only theory that holds is that her mouse slipped onto the correct name.

Jay took Jonathan Taylor at six, the exact spot where a guy sitting in a basement in Toledo would've taken him. Nobody was passed over. No board was read. Jay just walked into the room, pointed at the top name, and sat back down like he'd solved something.

Justin let the receiver run happen around him and then calmly took the best guy left, on time, at value. There's no crime here, which is itself suspicious. Somewhere the Substation Superstars war room is looking at each other trying to figure out who pressed it.

Mike wanted Jalen Hurts and wanted him now, so he stepped over James Cook III to get there. Nobody in this league was going to take Hurts. Nobody was even thinking about him. Mike bid against an empty chair and somehow came out behind.

Evan let James Cook III fall to him and then took him a beat later than the guy in the next league over would have. That's not patience, that's waiting for somebody else to make the decision and finding out nobody would. Courage of a man ordering the second thing on the menu.

For Chris Olave to work, Bree needs the injury history to end, the targets to spike, Breece Hall to disappoint her personally, and thirty guys she skipped to all have quiet years at the same time. That's not a draft pick, that's a prayer chain. Two receivers in, and the plan is already load-bearing on other people's failures.

Jesse needed a second running back and needed one badly enough to walk past fourteen better names to find one he liked the sound of. Ashton Jeanty was right there, doing nothing, hurting no one. Jesse looked at him and kept scrolling.

Nico Collins is expected to lead the Texans receivers after Jayden Higgins tore his ACL, and Chenell read that and decided it was worth stepping over CeeDee Lamb. The reigning champ is drafting off the injury report of guys who aren't even on her roster. Twenty-one better players stayed on the board so she could get the guy whose promotion came in a hospital.

Evan took Patrick Mahomes because he's Patrick Mahomes, seventy-two picks before some guy in a Denver bar would've bothered. He carries a QUESTIONABLE tag and a name so loud Evan couldn't hear it. Safest pick on the board, made unsafe entirely by Evan.

That's four quarterbacks for Mike, and Jaxson Dart is the newest one. He's part of a Giants trio that played eighteen snaps together last year, and analysts kept calling the whole group overvalued, so naturally Mike bought in. His roster can't run, can't catch, and can't put eleven guys on the grass at MetLife.

For Tetairoa McMillan to be right here, Carolina has to feed a rookie, Drake London has to stall out, Justin Herbert has to be a mirage, and eighteen guys Colin walked past all have to quietly agree to do nothing. Colin didn't draft a receiver, he drafted a set of conditions. Every one of them has to hold or the whole thing folds like a lawn chair.

Keshia took Jared Goff with nobody better on the board, which is now twice she's done the right thing and we still can't find the intent. That's four quarterbacks in a league that starts a couple. She's not building a roster anymore, she's running a quarterback pawn shop and occasionally accepting good inventory by mistake.

Jordan Love was sitting right there, doing nothing, bothering no one, and Tyler stepped over him and twenty-eight other guys to get DJ Moore. Three receivers in his last handful of picks, and this one cost him the most to get the least. He didn't shop the board, he grabbed the first name he recognized on the shelf.

Justin took a tight end eleven spots early with George Pickens and Davante Adams both still available, so the calm stretch is officially over. Two quarterbacks, one running back, one receiver, and now a Browns tight end. That's not a roster, that's a shelf of jerseys arranged by how much he likes the guy's name.

There isn't a room in this country where Tony Pollard goes at sixty-five, and Colin found the one chair in it and sat down. He passed George Kittle and Zay Flowers to do it. Two picks running now, Colin's drafting from a board only he can see, and the copium tank is getting a refill.

Bree already had a quarterback, then went and got Sam Darnold while George Kittle sat there being George Kittle. The prayer chain now includes Darnold's whole career reversing itself. Three receivers, two tight ends, and a backup quarterback taken thirteen better players early, because the plan needed one more thing to go wrong for somebody else.

Doug has five running backs and one receiver. Every Sunday he gets to pick which three backs sit and then stare at the one guy he owns who catches passes. Best player available, sure, but the shape of this team is a bowling ball with an arm glued on.

DK Metcalf works if the questionable tag means nothing, if Sam LaPorta was overrated, if Tee Higgins fades, and if twenty-one guys Chenell skipped all take the year off together. The reigning champ has now built a roster entirely out of medical paperwork and other people's bad luck. She's not reading a cheat sheet, she's reading charts.

Two quarterbacks and five receivers. Tyler has assembled a team that can throw the ball and catch the ball and has absolutely nobody to hand it to. Jameson Williams is the fifth guy running a route for a backfield that doesn't exist, and Rhamondre Stevenson watched the whole thing happen from the board.

James took Luther Burden III eleven spots early like it's the year the guy was a lock, walking past Rome Odunze and Tee Higgins to do it. Burden suffered a groin injury on August 8 in a contested red-zone rep. James saw the tape in his head, not the one from this summer.

Justin took Rome Odunze at eighty-two with nobody better on the board, which is the second time this draft he's accidentally been right. The jersey shelf now has a receiver on it who's actually good, and you can tell it wasn't planned because he took him on time. Whoever's pressing the button in the Substation Superstars war room, keep them away from the tight ends.

Mike finally took a receiver, and it's the one every guy in his fantasy chat had circled since July. Five quarterbacks and one running back, and the first brave thing he's done all draft is agree with a room full of people who already agreed. He's got a whole depth chart of passers and exactly one guy questionable enough to catch for them.

Evan starts two quarterbacks and owns one, so naturally he went and got a fourth running back. Rhamondre Stevenson started thirteen of fourteen games last year and still got out-touched by his own teammate, which is very much the Evan special: the guy who was almost the guy. He's not building a roster, he's collecting second choices.

James took TreVeyon Henderson, the back who out-touched Rhamondre Stevenson 25.1 percent to 18.9 in a New England committee, which is the first pick all draft he made off a real number instead of a memory. One quarterback in a league that starts two, and he keeps shopping in the backfield. The scary team is scary in the way a waiting room is scary.

Colin took Mark Andrews thirty-seven picks before anyone outside his house was going to, and this time the guy he can see on his private board is actually good. Best player available, correct position, no conditions attached, nothing that has to go wrong for four strangers. Somebody unplugged the copium tank and he panicked into being right.

Bree starts two quarterbacks, owns one and a Sam Darnold, and used this pick on her second running back. Three tight ends, though. The prayer chain has now expanded to include a rules change nobody has proposed.

Chenell took Jaylen Warren, a Steelers back, to go with the Steelers receiver she already grabbed off the charts. That's five running backs and zero quarterbacks for the reigning champ, and half of Pittsburgh's offense hanging in her closet. She's not drafting a team, she's assembling one road jersey at a time.
Round 9 and Jay still has 1 quarterback in a superflex league. Bold.

James now owns Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s teammate problem, because that's two Cardinals receivers fighting over the same football. He walked past twenty-six better guys to get there, including Christian Watson and T.J. Hockenson. The scary team is now a gift shop at State Farm Stadium.

Fifth receiver for Jay, one quarterback in a format that starts two, and Josh Jacobs still sitting on the board like furniture. He's got eleven better players behind him and a lineup he physically cannot fill out on Sunday. The guy who pointed at the top name in round one has spent nine rounds pointing at the wrong shelf.

Bree took Aaron Jones with nobody better on the board, on time, no strings, nothing that requires a stranger in another state to get hurt. The prayer chain got no new entries this round, which has to be unsettling for everybody on it. She drafted a healthy running back at his price and looked around like she'd broken a house rule.

Michael Pittman Jr. joins the closet, and the reigning champ now owns a questionable receiver to hedge a roster already built out of questionable receivers. She's not handcuffing a player, she's handcuffing a medical philosophy. One quarterback in a league that starts two, and every other slot is a second opinion.

Doug took Stefon Diggs and walked past eighteen guys to do it, including Josh Jacobs, who plays the position Doug apparently collects. The bowling ball has grown a second arm. He'll spend Sunday choosing which four running backs get to watch two receivers work.

Jesse has three quarterbacks, five running backs and two receivers, in that order of enthusiasm. He starts two passers and owns a third one just in case the other two get bored. The lineup he can actually field on Sunday has holes in it you could drive Josh Jacobs through, which is funny, because he just drafted him.

Seven running backs. Doug has seven running backs and two receivers, and Rachaad White makes it a roster where the depth chart is really just a list. The bowling ball's got arms coming out of everywhere now and still can't fill a flex without benching four guys.

Kenny Gainwell makes six running backs and still one quarterback in a format that starts two. The reigning champ has spent eleven rounds building the deepest bench in the league and a Sunday lineup with a hole in the middle of it. She'll be starting a running back at quarterback out of spite.

Third straight back for Bree, and this one she got eleven picks after everybody else was willing to pay. Nobody better was sitting there, nothing has to go wrong for a stranger in Washington, no rule needs rewriting. The prayer chain's been dismissed for the day and half of them don't know what to do with themselves.

Jay took Evan Engram forty-four picks before anyone with a computer would've, which is a long way to travel for a third tight end nobody asked about. Brian Thomas Jr. sat there the whole time. The guy who pointed at the top name in round one has now found a shelf so wrong it isn't even in the store.

James took MarShawn Lloyd with Brian Thomas Jr. sitting right there, which is twenty-four better guys walked past for a fourth running back. The scary team's gift shop has closed and reopened as a backfield with no exit. Still one quarterback in a league that starts two, and he keeps buying spare tires for a car with no engine.

Justin took Brian Thomas Jr. with nobody better available, on time, at the right spot, for the third time this draft. The jersey shelf is quietly turning into a wide receiver corps and you can tell nobody in that war room meant for it to happen. Two running backs, though. Somebody in there is going to notice eventually.

Jordan Addison is the right name at the right time, and he's also James's sixth receiver next to one quarterback in a league that starts two. Four backs, six wideouts, one guy who can throw it to any of them. The scary team has a skill position department and a staffing crisis, and James keeps hiring receptionists.

Colin took Jerry Jeudy twenty-six better players early, and Quentin Johnston sat there the whole time like a chair nobody wanted. The private board is back online and it's printing different names than everyone else's. That brief week where Colin was right about Mark Andrews is over, and the copium tank came back with a bigger hose.

Tyler took Wan'Dale Robinson with Khalil Shakir sitting right there, which is a sixth receiver for a team that owns one running back. He can field a route concept. He can't field a handoff. Somebody in that house needs to tell him the ball starts on the ground.

Jay's sixth receiver, taken twenty-six better players early, with one quarterback still on the roster in a format that starts two. He pointed at the top name in round one and hasn't found the quarterback aisle since. He's not shopping wrong anymore, he's wandering a store that closed.

Khalil Shakir, best guy on the board, correct spot, no argument available. That's three times now, and Keshia still has five quarterbacks in a league that starts two. The pawn shop's got a back room full of passers and a front counter with two receivers on it, and she keeps accidentally stocking the wrong one right.

Doug took Jalen Nailor twenty-nine better guys early, and Gunnar Helm watched him go. There isn't a room in Minnesota where that happens at 143. The bowling ball has stopped rolling and started making decisions.

Oronde Gadsden, with Chris Godwin Jr. sitting right there untouched. That's twenty-two better guys walked past for a second tight end on a roster that still has one quarterback. The gift shop, the backfield, now a tight end room, and James has built every department in the building except the one that opens the doors on Sunday.

Deebo Samuel is a fine pick, which for Evan means the fifth receiver on a team with three backs and three tight ends. Two quarterbacks, five guys to throw to, three more to throw to, and a running game that's mostly a rumor. He didn't collect a second choice this time, he just collected another one of the thing he already had eight of.

Evan took a defense in round fourteen with Romeo Doubs sitting there and seven hundred and ninety better players behind him. He's been ordering the second thing on the menu all draft and finally just pointed at the wall. Denver's whole defense counts as one player, so he's got that going for him.

James finished it off with the Seahawks defense and one quarterback in a league that starts two. He's got eleven guys who need somebody to throw them the ball and one arm in the building. The scary team's final move was hiring security for a store with nothing in it.

Colin took the Rams defense with Romeo Doubs sitting there and seven hundred and ninety-one better players behind him. The private board has finally scrolled past the part with names on it and landed on a logo. The copium tank is now hooked directly to eleven guys in blue who don't score points on purpose.

Jay took the Lions defense, which is his second unit of guys he can't start at quarterback in a format that starts two. One arm on the roster and a whole city of linebackers behind it. The store closed rounds ago and he's still in the parking lot picking up whatever's left on the pavement.

Bree took the Eagles defense with Romeo Doubs still sitting there and one quarterback on a roster in a league that starts two. Seven hundred and ninety-five better guys behind her, and she went and hired eleven strangers who all count as one. The prayer chain's back in session, and this time they're praying somebody teaches her the starting lineup rules.

Jesse already owns most of a backfield and now he's bought the Chargers defense to go with it. Six running backs, three quarterbacks, and a wall of jerseys arranged by nothing. Romeo Doubs sat there the entire time while Jesse shopped for a team logo.

For Brandon Aubrey to be worth this, Dallas has to stall out in field goal range roughly every drive, none of the seven hundred and ninety guys behind him can matter, and Jesse's third quarterback has to stay comfortable on the bench he was drafted for. He didn't take the first kicker off the board because he needed one. He took him because the scrolling had to stop somewhere.

Cameron Dicker over Romeo Doubs, which is Doug walking past seven hundred and ninety guys for a man whose job is to arrive after the offense fails. Seven running backs and now a specialist. The bowling ball has hired a placekicker to finish the drives its arms can't.

Jason Myers works if Seattle drives to the twenty-five and stops there all year, if the two tight ends and five backs sort themselves out, and if the reigning champ's one open Sunday slot fills itself in overnight. She built a roster out of medical paperwork and topped it with a guy who kicks. The charts didn't have a page for this, so she made one.

Bree took Ka'imi Fairbairn, which brings her to four tight ends, a kicker, a defense, and one quarterback in a format that starts two. Every slot on that roster is filled except the two that matter most. The prayer chain has been called back in and asked, very politely, whether a kicker can take snaps.

Eddy Pineiro, with Romeo Doubs still on the board doing nothing wrong. Jay's got six receivers, three tight ends and one arm to service all of them, and his answer was a guy who kicks. He walked past seven hundred and eighty-six better players in a store that's been dark since round nine.

James rounded out the scary team with Jake Bates. Six receivers, four backs, two tight ends, a defense, a kicker, and one quarterback in a league that starts two. Every department in the building is staffed, the lights are on, the sign is lit, and nobody has a key to the front door.
